2	name: gravity-ui
3	description: Builds, fixes, styles, and composes UI with the Gravity UI design system — the React ecosystem of @gravity-ui/* packages (uikit, charts, table, navigation, date-components, icons, and more). Routes to the correct package when look-alikes exist, applies theming and required setup, and prevents invented component APIs. Applies when working with @gravity-ui imports, uikit, ThemeProvider, --g- CSS tokens, or any prompt (EN or RU) mentioning gravity-ui, гравити, дизайн-система, компоненты, дашборд, таблица, график, or форма. Also installs required specialized Gravity UI packages when they are absent.
4	---
5	
6	# Building UI with Gravity UI
7	
8	Build UI on **real** Gravity UI components, not from memory. Gravity UI is a
9	multi-package React design system (`@gravity-ui/*`), so the two things that go
10	wrong are picking the wrong package and using an API from the wrong version.
11	This skill routes you to the right package, grounds you in the installed
12	version, and stops you from inventing APIs — match the installed versions and
13	follow the ecosystem catalog instead of guessing.
14	
15	## Efficiency guardrails
16	
17	- Do not read the same file twice. Reuse evidence already present in the session.
18	- Do not dump a reference file wholesale. Use targeted `rg -n -C 4` searches and keep each result below
19	  200 lines unless the whole file is necessary to resolve the task.
20	- Batch package, component, and symbol lookups into as few commands as possible.
21	- Stop documentation research as soon as package choice, import path, required setup, and uncertain props
22	  are confirmed. Documentation is evidence for decisions, not a checklist to read in full.
23	- Do not query unpkg, package source repositories, or alternative documentation mirrors.
24	- Do not install browsers or screenshot tooling, and do not start a dev server for routine verification,
25	  unless the user explicitly requests visual or browser verification.
26	- Run typecheck/build after implementation. If it fails, inspect only the failing API, fix it, and rerun
27	  the check. Do not repeatedly rebuild unchanged code.
28	
29	## Step 0 — pick the right package first (ecosystem routing)
30	
31	Before doing anything else, work out which `@gravity-ui/*` library the task
32	needs. Do not guess from training data — the ecosystem has look-alike packages
33	(`charts` vs `chartkit`, uikit `Table` vs `@gravity-ui/table`, `date-components`
34	vs `date-utils`, …) and picking the wrong one is the #1 failure.
35	Choose from the task's functionality, not only from dependencies already present in the project.
36	Open [`references/package-routing.md`](references/package-routing.md) and read
37	its top **first**: it opens with a task → package decision table that settles the
38	common cases (landing page, dashboard, data grid, calendar, charts, editor, app
39	shell, i18n), followed by the ecosystem catalog with a one-line "what it's for /
40	what to use instead" per package for everything else. Use it to choose the
41	package, then come back here for Step 1.
42	
43	Search the catalog for the task's relevant terms and read the matching package entries. Do not read the
44	entire catalog when its top and those entries are sufficient.
45	
46	Only after the package is chosen, run Step 1 to ground in that package's
47	installed version and API.
48	
49	## Step 1 — ground in the installed version of the chosen package
50	
51	1. **Read `package.json`.** Note each installed `@gravity-ui/*` package and its
52	   version. The installed version is the source of truth, not your memory.
53	   Resolve ranges from `node_modules` (`<pkg>/package.json` `version` field), not
54	   the range string in the root `package.json`.
55	
56	   If the chosen specialized package other than `@gravity-ui/uikit` is absent, add it with the project's
57	   existing package manager before importing it. Install its documented peer dependencies too, then
58	   resolve the installed version and continue with the local evidence below. Do not fall back to uikit,
59	   raw HTML, or a foreign library merely because the specialized package was initially absent. If
60	   installation is blocked, report the exact failure.
61	
62	2. **Fetch the docs for the package you are about to use, in this order,
63	   stopping at the first source that answers your question:**
64	
65	   (a) **LOCAL** — start with `node_modules/@gravity-ui/<pkg>/dist/docs/INDEX.md` or `node_modules/@gravity-ui/<pkg>/build/docs/INDEX.md`.
66	      If `INDEX.md` is absent for this package, fall back to the package's root `node_modules/@gravity-ui/<pkg>/README.md`.
67	      This is the *exact* installed version — always preferred for version-sensitive questions.
68	      Note: bundled docs are a recent addition — `uikit` ships `build/docs` only from **7.45.0**;
69	      older installs have no local docs at all, and that is expected, not an error. Go to (b).
70	      If an import, component, hook, or prop remains uncertain, inspect only its exact installed `.d.ts`
71	      before moving online. Batch all uncertain symbol lookups for that package.
72	   (b) **ONLINE** — per-package llms.txt at the **major line**:
73	      `https://gravity-ui.com/llms/<pkg>/<major>/llms.txt`
74	      (e.g. `/llms/uikit/7/llms.txt` for `^7.2.1`). The major-line URL serves the
75	      latest minor of that major — it tracks the major but not the exact patch.
76	      Use it when LOCAL has no docs for the package.
77	
78	3. **Fallback rule — never silently proceed on a failed or empty source:**
79	
80	   - If LOCAL has no README / `dist/docs` / `build/docs` for the package, or they are empty
81	     → fetch the ONLINE major-line llms.txt (b).
82	   - If the ONLINE request fails — network timeout, DNS, connection refused
83	     (air-gapped / corporate proxy), HTTP 404 (major not hosted), or an empty /
84	     non-markdown body → fall back to LOCAL README + dist/docs or build/docs (a).
85	   - **Do NOT use the `/llms/<pkg>/llms.txt` "latest" alias** as a fallback — it
86	     serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
87	     different API. The major-line URL is the versioned fallback; below it, go
88	     LOCAL, not "latest".
89	   - If BOTH are unreachable for a package → STOP and tell the user the
90	     package's docs are unreachable. Do not guess its API from training data.
91	
92	For a bounded local inspection, run:
93	
94	```sh
95	.agents/skills/gravity-ui/scripts/inspect-package.sh uikit Button Card Switch ThemeProvider
96	```
97	
98	The script reports the resolved version, available local documentation, and declaration files matching
99	the requested symbols. Read only the returned files needed to confirm an uncertain API.
100	
101	## Step 2 — implement on the chosen packages, then typecheck
102	
103	1. **Implement using only the `@gravity-ui/*` packages chosen in Step 0 and
104	   confirmed installed in Step 1.** Import from those packages exactly — do
105	   not substitute look-alike libraries (MUI, Ant, plain `<input>`) and do not
106	   reach for a `@gravity-ui/*` package that Step 1 did not confirm installed.
107	   Follow the prop APIs from the docs you just read, not memory; if a prop
108	   you want is not documented, it does not exist — use the documented one, or
109	   ask the user.
110	
111	2. **Apply the cross-cutting rules** in `rules/hallucination-traps.md` while
112	   writing: typography variants, the flex contract, theming/ladders,
113	   `Button view`, `Icon data`. Per-component traps live in the package's own
114	   `dist/docs`.
115	
116	3. **Typecheck before declaring done.** Run the project's typecheck command
117	   (typically `tsc --noEmit`; for monorepos, the workspace's typecheck script).
118	   Fix every error before reporting completion — a type error almost always
119	   means a wrong/invented prop, a wrong import path, or a version mismatch,
120	   which is precisely what Steps 0–1 were meant to prevent.
121	
122	   - If the typecheck surfaces a prop/path that contradicts the docs you read
123	     in Step 1, trust the **installed version** (the typechecker), not the
124	     docs snapshot — the docs may be from a different minor. Re-ground: read
125	     the package's `dist/docs/INDEX.md` in `node_modules` for the exact
126	     installed types.
127	   - If the typecheck is unavailable (no TS in the project), say so
128	     explicitly and ask the user how they want to verify; do not silently
129	     skip verification.
130	   - **Escape hatch.** If the user explicitly waived verification ("just
131	     sketch it", "quick prototype", "no need to check"), you may skip the
132	     typecheck — but state this plainly in your reply: *"typecheck skipped by
133	     user request — code is not verified"*. Do not skip silently.
134	   - **Know what typecheck does not cover.** A green `tsc` proves the API is
135	     real; it says nothing about layout or contrast. Before reporting done,
136	     say so, and either check or list for the user to check by hand: the
137	     screen in both `light` and `dark` themes (text and controls on colored
138	     fills especially), narrow (~375px) and wide (~1400px) viewports for
139	     horizontal overflow, and empty / loading / error states.
140	
141	## Hard rules
142	
143	- **`@gravity-ui/uikit` MUST be installed in every Gravity UI project.** It is
144	  the base component + design-token library every other `@gravity-ui/*` package
145	  builds on; without it components render unstyled. If `package.json` lacks it,
146	  stop and have the user install and configure it first (setup:
147	  `https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt`).
148	- **Read `package.json` before importing any `@gravity-ui/*` package.** Never
149	  assume a package is installed; never assume its major version.
150	- **Do not invent props or components.** Before using a component API you are
151	  not 100% sure of, check `rules/hallucination-traps.md` (ecosystem patterns)
152	  and the component's README in `dist/docs`. If still unsure, ask the user
153	  rather than guessing.
154	- **Never guess icon names** — they are hallucinated more often than not. To
155	  match an icon from a screenshot/photo/mock, run `scripts/icon-image-search.sh`
156	  (reverse image search). With only a description, look the name up on
157	  `gravity-ui.com/icons` or ask the user — do not invent one. Then pass it as an
158	  object (`<Icon data={CheckIcon} />`), never a string key. See
159	  `references/icons.md`.
160	- **Theming uses semantic `--g-*` tokens.** Never hardcode colors (`#fff`,
161	  `blue-500`); never hand-write `dark:` overrides. Full token tables live in
162	  `references/theming.md`; the cross-cutting traps (partial brand overrides,
163	  a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, controls on a brand background) live in
164	  `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
165	- **Required setup is package-specific** (style imports, `ThemeProvider`,
166	  peer-deps). It lives in each package's root README under "Required setup" —
167	  read it once per package, do not rely on memory.
168	
169	## What NOT to do
170	
171	These are the five most common ways agents break Gravity UI code. They are
172	already implied by the rules above; this section exists as an explicit
173	stop-sign. If you are about to do any of these, stop and re-ground.
174	
175	- **Do not substitute non-Gravity libraries.** No MUI, Ant Design, plain
176	  `<input>`/`<button>`, or look-alike component libs. Use the `@gravity-ui/*`
177	  package the task needs.
178	- **Do not invent component APIs or props.** If a prop is not in the docs you
179	  read in Step 1, it does not exist — do not write `variant=`, `color=`,
180	  `name=` (on `Icon`), or a `header-3` variant. Use the documented prop or
181	  ask the user. See `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
182	- **Do not use the `/llms/<pkg>/llms.txt` "latest" alias as a fallback.** It
183	  serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
184	  different API. The versioned online fallback is the major-line URL
185	  (`/llms/<pkg>/<major>/llms.txt`); below that, go LOCAL.
186	- **Do not partial-brand.** Setting only `--g-color-base-brand` leaves
187	  selection, focus, links and contrast on the default accent — a mismatched
188	  UI. Override the full brand token set, on each theme you support.
189	- **Do not override internal markup with `[class*='…']` / ID selectors.**
190	  That's written against one DOM structure and breaks silently when the
191	  component changes. Climb the customization ladder
192	  (global token → component CSS API → narrow flagged hack) before ever
193	  touching structure.
194	
195	## Deeper material — read on demand
196	
197	These files live alongside this SKILL.md and load only when relevant:
198	
199	- `references/package-routing.md` — offline snapshot of the ecosystem catalog
200	  (`gravity-ui.com/llms.txt`), refreshed each skill release. Used as the
201	  offline fallback in Step 0.
202	- `references/theming.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/theming.md`:
203	  `--g-*` token layers, `ThemeProvider`, branding, custom themes, scoped
204	  themes, `uikit-themer`. The bundled copy may lag — read
205	  `node_modules/@gravity-ui/uikit/build/docs/guides/theming.md` for the
206	  version-matched file.
207	- `references/layout.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/layout.md`:
208	  spacing scale (`--g-spacing-*`), `Flex`/`Box`, `Row`/`Col`/`Container`
209	  grid, breakpoints, `useLayoutContext`.
210	- `references/icons.md` — finding an icon by image
211	  (`scripts/icon-image-search.sh`) or on gravity-ui.com/icons; the
212	  object-vs-string rendering rule.
213	- `rules/hallucination-traps.md` — Incorrect/Correct pairs for the most
214	  commonly invented APIs: typography variants (`header-3..6` don't exist, no
215	  `Heading`), the flex contract (`min-width:0`, who shrinks), theming traps
216	  (partial brand overrides, a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, customization
217	  ladder), `Button view` not `variant`, `Icon data` not `name`. Per-component
218	  traps live in each package's `dist/docs`, not here.

56	
57	> If you need this library, read more at package [llms.txt](https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt)
58	> GitHub: [gravity-ui/uikit](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit)
59	
60	The base React component and design-token library for Gravity UI apps — controls, inputs, overlays, layout, and theming that every other @gravity-ui package builds on.
61	
62	#### When to use
63	
64	- Standard application UI: buttons, form controls, modals and popups, menus, tabs, labels, typography, and layout primitives.
65	- Selectable, navigable lists (`List`) and select controls (`Select`).
66	- The theming foundation of a Gravity UI app: `Provider`, design tokens, and CSS variables the rest of the `@gravity-ui/*` ecosystem expects to be present.

The `Table` component of uikit lives in `@gravity-ui/uikit/legacy` since v8 and is kept only for existing code.

81	A React component library for building AI chat interfaces, organized by Atomic Design (atoms → molecules → organisms → templates → pages) and SDK-agnostic — reach for it to assemble a chat UI (message lists, prompt input, tool calls, attachments) instead of composing those primitives out of `@gravity-ui/uikit` by hand.

# @gravity-ui/dashkit documentation

Documentation for the **installed** version of `@gravity-ui/dashkit`.
Your training data may be outdated — these files are the source of truth.

Paths are relative to this file (`node_modules/@gravity-ui/dashkit/build/docs/`).

## For AI agents

A dashboard grid composer that arranges resizable, draggable widgets in a responsive grid via a plugin system — reach for it when you build a user-editable dashboard (add/move/resize/delete widgets) instead of placing individual charts or panels by hand.

### When to use

- Rendering a configurable dashboard where widgets are positioned, resized, and rearranged on a grid (built on `react-grid-layout`).
- User-editable layouts: adding/removing widgets from an action panel, drag-and-drop, edit mode with overlay controls.
- Plugin-based widgets where each widget type (title, text, chart, custom) is registered once and driven by a `config`.

### When not to use

- For a single, fixed chart or panel, use [`@gravity-ui/charts`](https://gravity-ui.com/charts) or [`@gravity-ui/chartkit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/chartkit) directly — the grid/plugin machinery is overhead for one widget.
- For a general-purpose responsive grid that is not a widget dashboard, use `react-grid-layout` directly.
- For embedding ChartKit-backed chart widgets inside a DashKit dashboard, DashKit is the shell; it still relies on [`@gravity-ui/chartkit`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/chartkit) to render the actual charts.

### Common pitfalls

- **Hallucinated component `<Dashboard>`** — the export is `<DashKit>` (the drag-and-drop shell is `<DashKitDnDWrapper>` wrapping `<DashKit>` + `<ActionPanel>`).
- **Mutating `config` instead of using helpers** — use the static `DashKit.setItem({...})` / `DashKit.removeItem({...})` helpers to add/change/remove items so layout and ids stay consistent.
- **Forgetting `DashKit.setSettings` / `DashKit.registerPlugins`** — the component must be configured (language, grid settings, plugin registration) before it is rendered, or widgets show nothing.
- **Confusing the two param props** — `defaultGlobalParams` (dashboard-level defaults) vs `globalParams` (URL-overridable globals); both flow into the params generation queue consumed by ChartKit.
- **Calling `onChange` manually with the `change` event** — when you `event.preventDefault()` in the experimental `change` handler, DashKit keeps the visual state internally; re-setting `config.layout` from props resets that baseline.

## Install

```bash
npm i @gravity-ui/dashkit @gravity-ui/uikit
```

## Usage

### DashKit configuration

Before using `DashKit` as a react component, it must be configured.

- set language

  ```js
  import {configure, Lang} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';

  configure({lang: Lang.En});
  ```

- DashKit.setSettings

  Used for global DashKit settings (such as margins between widgets, default widget sizes and widget overlay menu)

  ```js
  import {DashKit} from '@gravity-ui/dashkit';

  DashKit.setSettings({
    gridLayout: {margin: [8, 8]},
    isMobile: true,
    // menu: [] as Array<MenuItem>,
  });
  ```

- DashKit.registerPlugins

  Registering and configuring plugins

  ```js
  import {DashKit} from '@gravity-ui/dashkit';
  import {pluginTitle, pluginText} from '@gravity-ui/dashkit';

  DashKit.registerPlugins(
    pluginTitle,
    pluginText.setSettings({
      apiHandler({text}) {
        return api.getMarkdown(text);
      },
    }),

268 {/* also outlined-contrast, flat-contrast */} 269

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
  One exception, legend kept: the tall segmented bar (*Figures* in `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`).
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |


## User Request

Building a React dashboard (Gravity UI DashKit) with KPI stat tiles and a small bar-chart widget inside draggable grid widgets

1	# Choosing a form
2	
3	Decide this **before** color. The data's job picks the form - and sometimes the
4	right form is not a chart.
5	
6	## Is it even a chart?
7	
8	| The data is... | Use | Not |
9	|---|---|---|
10	| A single current value (+ maybe a trend) | **Stat tile** (value + delta + sparkline) | A one-bar bar chart |
11	| A handful of headline numbers | **KPI row** of stat tiles | A grouped bar chart |
12	| The one number a dashboard leads with | **Hero figure** (>=48px, sans) | - |
13	| A single ratio against a limit | **Meter** (same-ramp track) | A pie of 2 slices |
14	| One whole split into <= 6 parts, read at a glance, standing alone | **Tall segmented bar** (to compare the parts instead -> *Part-to-whole - which bar* below) | A donut or a pie |
15	| More than ~7 classes that all carry meaning | A **table** (or table + chart) | More colors |
16	
17	If a chart *is* right, pick the type by the job:
18	
19	## The job -> the type
20	
21	| Job (what the reader must do) | Default form | Color job |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| Compare magnitude, low -> high | bar / column; **heatmap** for a grid | sequential (one hue) |
24	| Trend over time | line; area for a single series | sequential or 1 categorical |
25	| Tell distinct series apart | grouped/stacked bar, multi-line | **categorical** |
26	| One series is the point, rest are context | **emphasis** (highlight one, gray the rest) | 1 hue + gray |
27	| Above/below a baseline; delta to target | diverging bar, or line vs baseline | diverging |
28	| Part-to-whole | a bar; which one -> *Part-to-whole - which bar* below | categorical; one hue for ranked bars |
29	| Ordered-scale share (Likert, sentiment, agree<->disagree) | **diverging stacked bar**, centered on neutral | diverging |
30	| Before -> after per item | dumbbell | 1 hue, 2 shades |
31	
32	## The rules behind the table
33	
34	- **Sequential is the safe default.** One hue, more-is-darker. It stays legible and
35	  consistent and is hard to misread. Reach for it unless the data's job is
36	  specifically *identity* or *polarity*.
37	- **Categorical is for when the series ARE the subject** - and it has a real cost:
38	  it can bury the one data point that actually matters. If the story is "this one
39	  went up," that's **emphasis**, not categorical.
40	- **Emphasis** = the most underused form. One series in the accent hue, the rest in
41	  the de-emphasis gray. Often the honest answer to "make this chart clearer."
42	- **Texture is an opt-in expression, not a default form.** It earns its place only
43	  for accessibility (full CVD), print/export, and `forced-colors`. Never decorative.
44	  -> see `marks-and-anatomy.md`.
45	
46	## Part-to-whole - which bar
47	
48	A request for a donut or a pie is usually a part-to-whole request (one ratio against a
49	limit is a **Meter**, above). Answer it with one of these; the donut stays deprioritized.
50	
51	| The reader must... | Use |
52	|---|---|
53	| Compare the parts with each other, rank them, tell close values apart, or read more than 6 parts | **Ranked horizontal bars**, one per part, largest first, one hue: bars on one baseline compare more exactly than segments laid end to end |
54	| See how one whole splits, at a glance: one bar alone in a card, no figures listed beside it | **Tall segmented bar**: each part its own block, its share or amount printed on it where it fits, and a legend of names only. <= 6 parts; fold a tail nobody needs to read into "Other" |
55	| Read the split beside its figures: down the rows of a table or list, or above a list that already gives each part's name and amount | **Thin segmented bar**, no text: the text beside it carries the figures the reader needs, and printing them on the bar adds nothing. One legend for the whole table; a swatch on each list row replaces the legend |
56	| See the split change over time, or compare several wholes on one shared axis | **Stacked bar chart** (go horizontal for many / long-named categories): its axis carries the values |
57	
58	Specs for the two segmented bars -> *Figures* in `marks-and-anatomy.md`.
59	
60	## Series-count ladder (categorical)
61	
62	| Series | Treatment |
63	|---|---|
64	| 1-3 | color alone is comfortable for everyone; direct-label |
65	| 4 | adjacent forms (stacks, bars, lines) stay gate-safe, but direct labels become mandatory - yellow and orange now share the screen; all-pairs forms (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small multiples) cap at **three** - fold to "Other" or facet rather than seat a 4th |
66	| 5-6 | soft cap; legend or small multiples |
67	| 7-8 | token ceiling; past it, fold the tail into "Other," facet into small multiples, or use composite encoding (hue × shape) |
68	
69	Never solve "too many series" by generating more hues. A generated 9th hue is
70	indistinguishable from an existing one under CVD and breaks every check.
71

1	# Reference palette
2	
3	This is the **reference instance** of the data-viz method: every parameter the
4	method needs, filled in with a validated default palette. The rest of the skill
5	is system-agnostic - **to target your brand, substitute this file's values** and
6	re-run the validator. Nothing else changes.
7	
8	## How to use these values
9	
10	Everything below is plain hex. In an HTML chart, **define the slots you use as
11	CSS custom properties in a local `<style>` block** at the top of the file, then
12	reference them by role throughout - so the light/dark values swap in one place,
13	and the chart body is written against roles rather than raw hex:
14	
15	```css
16	.viz-root {
17	  color-scheme: light;
18	  --surface-1:      #fcfcfb;   /* chart surface */
19	  --text-primary:   #0b0b0b;
20	  --text-secondary: #52514e;
21	  --series-1:       #2a78d6;   /* categorical slot 1 */
22	  /* ...only the roles this chart uses */
23	}
24	@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
25	  :root:where(:not([data-theme="light"])) .viz-root {
26	    color-scheme: dark;
27	    --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
28	    --text-primary:   #f0efec;
29	    --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
30	    --series-1:       #3987e5;
31	  }
32	}
33	:root[data-theme="dark"] .viz-root {
34	  color-scheme: dark;
35	  --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
36	  --text-primary:   #f0efec;
37	  --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
38	  --series-1:       #3987e5;
39	}
40	```
41	
42	Declare the dark values under both scopes as above - the media query covers
43	the OS setting; the `data-theme` scope covers the viewer's theme toggle,
44	which must win both ways (the `:not(...)` guard lets a light stamp beat
45	OS-dark; `:where()` keeps the media block below the toggle scope).
46	
47	## Categorical palette
48	
49	Both modes are selected. The dark column is the same eight hues stepped for the
50	dark surface, not a separate palette:
51	
52	| Slot | Hue | Light | Dark |
53	|------|-----|-------|------|
54	| 1 | blue | `#2a78d6` | `#3987e5` |
55	| 2 | orange | `#eb6834` | `#d95926` |
56	| 3 | aqua | `#1baf7a` | `#199e70` |
57	| 4 | yellow | `#eda100` | `#c98500` |
58	| 5 | magenta | `#e87ba4` | `#d55181` |
59	| 6 | green | `#008300` | `#008300` |
60	| 7 | violet | `#6250d6` | `#9085e9` |
61	| 8 | red | `#e34948` | `#e66767` |
62	
63	This order passes every hard gate in both modes on the default *adjacent*
64	pairlist (stacks, bars, lines): worst adjacent CVD Delta E 9.1 light / 8.4 dark
65	(OKLab ×100, >=8 target), worst adjacent normal-vision Delta E 19.6 light / 19.3
66	dark (>=15 floor). Under `--pairs all` (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small
67	multiples) the full eight cannot clear the floors - with all 28 pairs in
68	play no ordering can (the pairlist no longer depends on order), and
69	re-stepping is off the table by the documented-palette rule - so those
70	chart forms carry a series cap: **the first three slots validate all-pairs
71	in both modes** (worst pair CVD Delta E 9.2 light / 9.4 dark, normal-vision 24.0
72	light / 20.9 dark - clear of the CVD warn band). Past three, fold to "Other" or
73	facet: the fourth slot puts yellow and orange on screen
74	together, and that pair fails the all-pairs floors (normal-vision 13.7
75	light; CVD 4.8 dark). Three light-mode slots (magenta, yellow, aqua)
76	sit below 3:1 contrast on the light surface: the **relief rule** applies (ship
77	visible direct labels or the table view). The dark steps were chosen for the
78	dark band (OKLCH L ~ 0.48-0.67, >= 3:1 on the dark surface) and validated as a
79	set. (Ordering history: adopted July 2026 for its more harmonious opening -
80	the same eight hues and steps as its predecessor, re-ordered, zero hex
81	changes. The predecessor validated its first FOUR slots all-pairs, with its
82	dark run in the 6-8 CVD warn band, so secondary encoding was required there;
83	this order deliberately trades that fourth slot - yellow now sits beside orange -
84	for better-looking leading colors. Revisit the trade if yellow<->orange
85	confusion shows up in real charts with four or more series; undoing it is a
86	pure re-order. Light slot 7 has since been lightened, `#4a3aa7` -> `#6250d6`
87	(August 2026); the adjacent-pair figures above are unchanged by that move, the
88	non-adjacent blue<->violet pair now sits below both floors under `--pairs all`
89	(normal-vision 10.5, CVD 4.5 - inside the range the series cap already
90	excludes), and the order enumeration was run with the earlier value.) When you
91	swap in your own ramps, hold your palette to the full gate.
92	
93	The slot **ordering** is the CVD-safety mechanism, not cosmetic - candidate
94	orderings were enumerated and only those clearing every adjacent gate in both
95	modes kept (see `color-formula.md` § Themes); this default is one of the
96	passing orders, picked among them for its opening colors. When you swap in
97	your brand's hues, do the same: run the validator on candidate orderings and
98	choose only among the passing ones.
99	
100	## Sequential hue
101	
102	Default single hue: **blue**, light->dark. When two sequential contexts appear at
103	once, the second takes the next categorical slot's hue (orange), each as its own
104	one-hue ramp.
105	
106	| step | hex | step | hex | step | hex | step | hex |
107	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
108	| 100 | `#cde2fb` | 250 | `#86b6ef` | 400 | `#3987e5` | 550 | `#1c5cab` |
109	| 150 | `#b7d3f6` | 300 | `#6da7ec` | 450 | `#2a78d6` | 600 | `#184f95` |
110	| 200 | `#9ec5f4` | 350 | `#5598e7` | 500 | `#256abf` | 650 | `#104281` |
111	| | | | | | | 700 | `#0d366b` |
112	
113	The full 100->700 range is for **sequential** encoding (continuous magnitude -
114	heatmaps, choropleths) where the lightest step means "near zero" and is allowed
115	to recede toward the surface. For an **ordinal** ramp (discrete ordered marks -
116	funnel stages, tiers - validated with `--ordinal`), the step nearest the surface
117	must still clear 2:1: on light, start no lighter than **step 250** (`#86b6ef`,
118	2.06:1); on dark, go no darker than **step 600** (`#184f95`, 2.15:1).
119	
120	## Diverging pair
121	
122	**blue <-> red** - warm/cool poles that read as opposite. Neutral midpoint is gray
123	(light `#f0efec`, dark `#383835`). Equal step count per arm. (blue<->aqua was
124	rejected - both cool, the midpoint doesn't read as "nothing".)
125	
126	## Status palette (fixed - never themed)
127	
128	| role | hex | light-surface contrast | dark-surface contrast |
129	|---|---|---|---|
130	| good | `#0ca30c` | 3.27 | 5.19 |
131	| warning | `#fab219` | 1.79 | 9.49 |
132	| serious | `#ec835a` | 2.57 | 6.60 |
133	| critical | `#d03b3b` | 4.68 | 3.62 |
134	
135	Dark: same four steps - all clear 3:1 on the dark surface (`#1a1a19`) and remain
136	distinct from the dark categorical slots. On the light surface, warning and
137	serious are sub-3:1 by design; the **icon + label** pairing is the mitigation, so
138	a status color never carries meaning alone. These steps are deliberately distinct
139	from the categorical slots so a status color never impersonates a series -
140	distinct enough that nothing collides at a glance, not enough for hue to
141	carry the distinction unaided: measured by the series floor's own bar
142	(unsimulated Delta E >= 15), around nine categorical-vs-status pairs per mode sit
143	below 15 - in light mode red vs critical and yellow vs warning both measure
144	4.8, slot-2 orange sits 5.8 from status-serious, and the light success text
145	green `#006300` sits 10.1 from the series green; green vs status-good (9.7)
146	holds in both modes, since both hexes are mode-invariant. The rule is general: any series color beside a
147	same-hue-family status or delta cue leans on the icon + label pairing and on
148	placement; never on hue alone.
149	
150	## Texture fill (the accessibility channel)
151	
152	One hand-drawn **"Lines"** fill, used at **45° and its 135° mirror only**. Inked
153	tone-on-tone (a darker step of the fill's own ramp). On value scales it is
154	*ordered* (rotation steps with magnitude; arm angle carries the diverging sign).
155	Triggered by the accessibility setting, print, or `forced-colors` - never
156	decorative, never on by default.
157	
158	## Surfaces (for the validator)
159	
160	- Light chart surface: `#fcfcfb`
161	- Dark chart surface: `#1a1a19`
162	
163	These are the validator's built-in defaults. **When you swap in your own
164	palette, re-run against your own surfaces:**
165	`--surface <your-light> --mode light` and `--surface <your-dark> --mode dark` -
166	contrast and band results are only meaningful against the surface the chart
167	actually renders on.
168	
169	## Chart chrome & ink
170	
171	| Role | Light | Dark |
172	|---|---|---|
173	| Chart surface | `#fcfcfb` | `#1a1a19` |
174	| Page plane | `#f9f9f7` | `#0d0d0d` |
175	| Primary ink | `#0b0b0b` | `#f0efec` |
176	| Secondary ink | `#52514e` | `#c3c2b7` |
177	| Muted (axis/labels) | `#898781` | `#898781` |
178	| Label inside a categorical or status fill | `#ffffff`, except `#0b0b0b` on yellow and warning | `#ffffff`, except `#0b0b0b` on warning |
179	| Gridline (hairline) | `#e1e0d9` | `#2c2c2a` |
180	| Baseline / axis | `#c3c2b7` | `#383835` |
181	| Delta up good (success text) | `#006300` | `#0ca30c` |
182	| Border (hairline ring) | `rgba(11,11,11,0.10)` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.10)` |
183	
184	## Filter controls
185	
186	Filters are standard UI, not chart components - the chart layer only adds the
187	composition rules in `interaction.md`. A date-range control is a list of preset
188	rows (today, last 7/30/90 days, month-to-date) with selection marked by a 16px
189	bold check, hover as a ghost wash, and custom range behind a hairline in the
190	footer. Dimension filters are a standard combobox.
191	
192	## Typeface & figures
193	
194	Everything - including the hero figure - stays in the system sans: `system-ui,
195	-apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`. No display or serif face anywhere. Large
196	standalone numbers (hero figure, stat-tile values) use the default proportional
197	figures; reserve `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for columns that must align
198	vertically (table rows, axis ticks). Substitute your brand's UI sans here.
199

30	    --series-1:       #3987e5;
31	  }
32	}

34	  color-scheme: dark;
35	  --surface-1:      #1a1a19;

41	
42	Declare the dark values under both scopes as above - the media query covers
43	the OS setting; the `data-theme` scope covers the viewer's theme toggle,
44	which must win both ways (the `:not(...)` guard lets a light stamp beat
45	OS-dark; `:where()` keeps the media block below the toggle scope).
46	
47	## Categorical palette
48	
49	Both modes are selected. The dark column is the same eight hues stepped for the
50	dark surface, not a separate palette:
51	
52	| Slot | Hue | Light | Dark |
53	|------|-----|-------|------|
54	| 1 | blue | `#2a78d6` | `#3987e5` |
55	| 2 | orange | `#eb6834` | `#d95926` |
56	| 3 | aqua | `#1baf7a` | `#199e70` |
57	| 4 | yellow | `#eda100` | `#c98500` |
58	| 5 | magenta | `#e87ba4` | `#d55181` |
59	| 6 | green | `#008300` | `#008300` |
60	| 7 | violet | `#6250d6` | `#9085e9` |
61	| 8 | red | `#e34948` | `#e66767` |
62	
63	This order passes every hard gate in both modes on the default *adjacent*
64	pairlist (stacks, bars, lines): worst adjacent CVD Delta E 9.1 light / 8.4 dark
65	(OKLab ×100, >=8 target), worst adjacent normal-vision Delta E 19.6 light / 19.3
66	dark (>=15 floor). Under `--pairs all` (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small
67	multiples) the full eight cannot clear the floors - with all 28 pairs in
68	play no ordering can (the pairlist no longer depends on order), and
69	re-stepping is off the table by the documented-palette rule - so those
70	chart forms carry a series cap: **the first three slots validate all-pairs
71	in both modes** (worst pair CVD Delta E 9.2 light / 9.4 dark, normal-vision 24.0
72	light / 20.9 dark - clear of the CVD warn band). Past three, fold to "Other" or
73	facet: the fourth slot puts yellow and orange on screen
74	together, and that pair fails the all-pairs floors (normal-vision 13.7
75	light; CVD 4.8 dark). Three light-mode slots (magenta, yellow, aqua)
76	sit below 3:1 contrast on the light surface: the **relief rule** applies (ship
77	visible direct labels or the table view). The dark steps were chosen for the
78	dark band (OKLCH L ~ 0.48-0.67, >= 3:1 on the dark surface) and validated as a
79	set. (Ordering history: adopted July 2026 for its more harmonious opening -
80	the same eight hues and steps as its predecessor, re-ordered, zero hex
81	changes. The predecessor validated its first FOUR slots all-pairs, with its
82	dark run in the 6-8 CVD warn band, so secondary encoding was required there;
83	this order deliberately trades that fourth slot - yellow now sits beside orange -
84	for better-looking leading colors. Revisit the trade if yellow<->orange
85	confusion shows up in real charts with four or more series; undoing it is a
86	pure re-order. Light slot 7 has since been lightened, `#4a3aa7` -> `#6250d6`
87	(August 2026); the adjacent-pair figures above are unchanged by that move, the
88	non-adjacent blue<->violet pair now sits below both floors under `--pairs all`
89	(normal-vision 10.5, CVD 4.5 - inside the range the series cap already
90	excludes), and the order enumeration was run with the earlier value.) When you
91	swap in your own ramps, hold your palette to the full gate.
92	
93	The slot **ordering** is the CVD-safety mechanism, not cosmetic - candidate
94	orderings were enumerated and only those clearing every adjacent gate in both
95	modes kept (see `color-formula.md` § Themes); this default is one of the
96	passing orders, picked among them for its opening colors. When you swap in
97	your brand's hues, do the same: run the validator on candidate orderings and
98	choose only among the passing ones.
99	
100	## Sequential hue
101	
102	Default single hue: **blue**, light->dark. When two sequential contexts appear at
103	once, the second takes the next categorical slot's hue (orange), each as its own
104	one-hue ramp.
105	
106	| step | hex | step | hex | step | hex | step | hex |
107	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
108	| 100 | `#cde2fb` | 250 | `#86b6ef` | 400 | `#3987e5` | 550 | `#1c5cab` |
109	| 150 | `#b7d3f6` | 300 | `#6da7ec` | 450 | `#2a78d6` | 600 | `#184f95` |
110	| 200 | `#9ec5f4` | 350 | `#5598e7` | 500 | `#256abf` | 650 | `#104281` |
111	| | | | | | | 700 | `#0d366b` |
112	
113	The full 100->700 range is for **sequential** encoding (continuous magnitude -
114	heatmaps, choropleths) where the lightest step means "near zero" and is allowed
115	to recede toward the surface. For an **ordinal** ramp (discrete ordered marks -
116	funnel stages, tiers - validated with `--ordinal`), the step nearest the surface
117	must still clear 2:1: on light, start no lighter than **step 250** (`#86b6ef`,
118	2.06:1); on dark, go no darker than **step 600** (`#184f95`, 2.15:1).
119	
120	## Diverging pair
121	
122	**blue <-> red** - warm/cool poles that read as opposite. Neutral midpoint is gray
123	(light `#f0efec`, dark `#383835`). Equal step count per arm. (blue<->aqua was
124	rejected - both cool, the midpoint doesn't read as "nothing".)
125	
126	## Status palette (fixed - never themed)
127	
128	| role | hex | light-surface contrast | dark-surface contrast |
129	|---|---|---|---|
130	| good | `#0ca30c` | 3.27 | 5.19 |
131	| warning | `#fab219` | 1.79 | 9.49 |
132	| serious | `#ec835a` | 2.57 | 6.60 |
133	| critical | `#d03b3b` | 4.68 | 3.62 |
134	
135	Dark: same four steps - all clear 3:1 on the dark surface (`#1a1a19`) and remain
136	distinct from the dark categorical slots. On the light surface, warning and
137	serious are sub-3:1 by design; the **icon + label** pairing is the mitigation, so
138	a status color never carries meaning alone. These steps are deliberately distinct
139	from the categorical slots so a status color never impersonates a series -
140	distinct enough that nothing collides at a glance, not enough for hue to
141	carry the distinction unaided: measured by the series floor's own bar
142	(unsimulated Delta E >= 15), around nine categorical-vs-status pairs per mode sit
143	below 15 - in light mode red vs critical and yellow vs warning both measure
144	4.8, slot-2 orange sits 5.8 from status-serious, and the light success text

146	holds in both modes, since both hexes are mode-invariant. The rule is general: any series color beside a
147	same-hue-family status or delta cue leans on the icon + label pairing and on
148	placement; never on hue alone.
149	
150	## Texture fill (the accessibility channel)
151	
152	One hand-drawn **"Lines"** fill, used at **45° and its 135° mirror only**. Inked
153	tone-on-tone (a darker step of the fill's own ramp). On value scales it is
154	*ordered* (rotation steps with magnitude; arm angle carries the diverging sign).
155	Triggered by the accessibility setting, print, or `forced-colors` - never
156	decorative, never on by default.
157	
158	## Surfaces (for the validator)
159	
160	- Light chart surface: `#fcfcfb`
161	- Dark chart surface: `#1a1a19`
162	
163	These are the validator's built-in defaults. **When you swap in your own
164	palette, re-run against your own surfaces:**
165	`--surface <your-light> --mode light` and `--surface <your-dark> --mode dark` -
166	contrast and band results are only meaningful against the surface the chart
167	actually renders on.
168	
169	## Chart chrome & ink
170	
171	| Role | Light | Dark |
172	|---|---|---|
173	| Chart surface | `#fcfcfb` | `#1a1a19` |
174	| Page plane | `#f9f9f7` | `#0d0d0d` |
175	| Primary ink | `#0b0b0b` | `#f0efec` |
176	| Secondary ink | `#52514e` | `#c3c2b7` |
177	| Muted (axis/labels) | `#898781` | `#898781` |
178	| Label inside a categorical or status fill | `#ffffff`, except `#0b0b0b` on yellow and warning | `#ffffff`, except `#0b0b0b` on warning |
179	| Gridline (hairline) | `#e1e0d9` | `#2c2c2a` |
180	| Baseline / axis | `#c3c2b7` | `#383835` |
181	| Delta up good (success text) | `#006300` | `#0ca30c` |
182	| Border (hairline ring) | `rgba(11,11,11,0.10)` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.10)` |
183	
184	## Filter controls
185	
186	Filters are standard UI, not chart components - the chart layer only adds the
187	composition rules in `interaction.md`. A date-range control is a list of preset
188	rows (today, last 7/30/90 days, month-to-date) with selection marked by a 16px
189	bold check, hover as a ghost wash, and custom range behind a hairline in the
190	footer. Dimension filters are a standard combobox.
191	
192	## Typeface & figures
193	
194	Everything - including the hero figure - stays in the system sans: `system-ui,
195	-apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`. No display or serif face anywhere. Large
196	standalone numbers (hero figure, stat-tile values) use the default proportional
197	figures; reserve `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for columns that must align
198	vertically (table rows, axis ticks). Substitute your brand's UI sans here.

1	# Marks & anatomy
2	
3	The quiet, considered look is a few fixed specs plus two pieces of negative space.
4	The data is the only thing allowed to be loud.
5	
6	## Mark specs (fixed across every chart)
7	
8	| Mark | Spec |
9	|---|---|
10	| Bar / column | **<= 24px thick** (cap it - never fill the slot; let the band's leftover be air); **4px rounded data-end, square at the baseline**; grows from a single baseline |
11	| Line | **2px**, round join/cap |
12	| Marker / end-dot | **>= 8px** (r >= 4), filled with the series color |
13	| Area fill | the series hue at **~10% opacity** (a wash, never a saturated block) |
14	| Gridlines / axes | one-step-off-surface gray, **hairline (1px), solid** (never dashed), recessive |
15	
16	## The two spacers (white doing the separating)
17	
18	- **Surface gap.** A **2px gap** in the surface color separates touching marks - every
19	  segment of a stacked bar, and every adjacent (touching) bar, the same width. Keep it
20	  one consistent width across a stack; neighbors one step apart read distinct because of
21	  the gap, not a stroke drawn around them.
22	- **Surface ring.** Dots and end-markers carry a **2px ring in the surface color**,
23	  so they stay legible where they cross a line or overlap each other. The ring is part
24	  of the mark's hover/hit target, not just spacing - see `interaction.md` (small dots
25	  are easy to under-size for hover).
26	
27	Never draw a border around a mark to separate it. The gap and the ring are the
28	mechanism; a stroke adds data-weight ink that isn't data.
29	
30	## Labels & legend
31	
32	A **legend is always present for two or more series** - the dependable identity
33	channel; never make the reader rely on color-matching alone. Direct labels then ride
34	the marks to *supplement* it. **A single series needs no legend box**: there is only
35	one color, so the chart's title or subtitle already says what is plotted. A box with
36	one swatch restates the title and costs space.
37	
38	- **Label selectively - never a number on every point.** A value beside every dot or
39	  segment is chaos and goes unread. Label the endpoint, the extreme, or the one series
40	  the story is about; let the axis, the legend, and the tooltip/table carry the rest.
41	  Direct labels work *because* they are sparing - flood the chart and they stop working.
42	- **Direct labels before gridlines; gridlines before a second axis.**
43	- **A label that won't fit doesn't get clipped - measure first.** Only place a label
44	  *inside* a bar or stacked segment when the rendered text fits with comfortable
45	  padding on both sides. If it doesn't fit: for a whole bar/column, move the label
46	  outside the bar end (or to the tooltip if there's no room outside either); for an
47	  *interior* stacked segment (which has no free end),
48	  skip the inline label and let the legend + tooltip carry it. Either way the value
49	  stays in the table view, so nothing is gated. Never use `overflow: hidden` on the
50	  segment to "solve" it - that crops the first/last characters and is worse than no
51	  label. Text never overflows or is clipped by its own mark.
52	- Bars -> value at the tip. Columns -> value on the cap. Lines -> value at the end.
53	- Y-axis ticks: round to clean numbers, in full under 10,000 (0 / 1,000 / 2,000) and
54	  compact on an axis that reaches it (0 / 10K / 20K), one style per axis; along a
55	  horizontal axis, in full under a million where the labels fit side by side. They
56	  carry the values you didn't directly label, so keep them unless every value is labeled.
57	- **Text never wears the data color.** Marks - bars, lines, dots, area fills - carry
58	  the series color; labels, values, legends, and axis text use **text tokens**
59	  (primary / secondary / muted). A light categorical hue (yellow, aqua) is illegible
60	  as text on the surface. Identity comes from the colored mark *beside* the text - a
61	  dot, a short line-key, a swatch - never from coloring the text itself. A label set
62	  *inside* a colored fill (a stacked segment, a map tile) is the one exception: white or
63	  near-black, the same two in both modes, by the fill's luminance. `palette.md` says which its
64	  categorical and status colors take.
65	- **When end-labels collide, don't stack them.** Direct end-labels work when series
66	  separate at the right edge. When lines converge, nudging labels apart vertically
67	  detaches them from their lines and reads as noise - instead use **leader lines**
68	  (a thin connector from label to line-end), facet into **small multiples**, or fall
69	  back to the legend + tooltip. Past ~4 converging series, small multiples is usually right.
70	
71	## Figures - when the form is a number
72	
73	- **Stat tile** contract: `label` (sentence case, no trailing colon) · `value` (Sans
74	  semibold, auto-compact: 1,284 / 12.9K / $4.2M) · `delta` (optional; signed,
75	  vs a named period; color = direction × whether up is good) · `trend` (optional;
76	  12-point sparkline in the de-emphasis hue, current period in the accent).
77	- **Meter:** the fill carries severity (accent -> warning -> danger); the unfilled
78	  track is a **lighter step of the same ramp** (blue-on-blue, etc.) so state reads
79	  across the whole bar.
80	- **Segmented bar - one whole, split into parts.** A figure, thin or tall, with no baseline, so
81	  no end is square. Widths proportional to the values; a part at zero draws nothing.
82	  **Thin:** 8px, or 4px in dense rows; fully rounded ends; no text. **Tall:** 28px and never
83	  more; each part its own block, 4px corners, its share (46%) or rounded amount (413M)
84	  printed inside at the leading edge, in white or near-black (*Labels & legend* says which).
85	  A block too narrow for its label prints none: that value stays in the table view.
86	  Hover, keyboard focus, and the bar's accessible name give every part's name, amount, and
87	  share. The legend lists the names in block order and repeats no numbers. The tall bar is
88	  exempt from four chart rules: the 24px bar cap, the ban on large saturated blocks, the ban
89	  on a number on every point, and direct name labels (its legend names the parts). It keeps
90	  its legend and its table view.
91	- **Hero figure.** The single number a dashboard leads with, >=48px, in the same
92	  sans as everything else (never a display or serif face - it reads as off-brand
93	  decoration). Exactly one per view.
94	- **Proportional figures for big numbers; tabular only in columns.** A large
95	  standalone value (hero figure, stat-tile value) uses the font's default
96	  proportional figures - `tabular-nums` gives every digit the width of a `0`, so a
97	  number like `121` looks loose at display sizes. Reserve
98	  `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for columns of numbers that must align
99	  vertically (table rows, axis ticks).
100	
101	## Texture - the backup channel (opt-in)
102	
103	Where hue fails - full-severity CVD, grayscale print, `forced-colors` - texture
104	carries identity. One directional hand-drawn fill, used at **45° and its 135° mirror
105	only** (never horizontal/vertical - those read as gridlines/bars). Inked tone-on-tone
106	(a step from the fill's own ramp), equal loudness across slots. On value scales the
107	texture is *ordered* (rotation steps with magnitude; arm angle carries the diverging
108	sign) so it never misstates the value. Triggered by an accessibility setting, print,
109	or `forced-colors` - never on by default. (See `palette.md`.)

76	  12-point sparkline in the de-emphasis hue, current period in the accent).
77	- **Meter:** the fill carries severity (accent -> warning -> danger); the unfilled
78	  track is a **lighter step of the same ramp** (blue-on-blue, etc.) so state reads
79	  across the whole bar.
80	- **Segmented bar - one whole, split into parts.** A figure, thin or tall, with no baseline, so
81	  no end is square. Widths proportional to the values; a part at zero draws nothing.
82	  **Thin:** 8px, or 4px in dense rows; fully rounded ends; no text. **Tall:** 28px and never
83	  more; each part its own block, 4px corners, its share (46%) or rounded amount (413M)
84	  printed inside at the leading edge, in white or near-black (*Labels & legend* says which).
85	  A block too narrow for its label prints none: that value stays in the table view.
86	  Hover, keyboard focus, and the bar's accessible name give every part's name, amount, and
87	  share. The legend lists the names in block order and repeats no numbers. The tall bar is
88	  exempt from four chart rules: the 24px bar cap, the ban on large saturated blocks, the ban
89	  on a number on every point, and direct name labels (its legend names the parts). It keeps
90	  its legend and its table view.
91	- **Hero figure.** The single number a dashboard leads with, >=48px, in the same
92	  sans as everything else (never a display or serif face - it reads as off-brand
93	  decoration). Exactly one per view.
94	- **Proportional figures for big numbers; tabular only in columns.** A large
95	  standalone value (hero figure, stat-tile value) uses the font's default
96	  proportional figures - `tabular-nums` gives every digit the width of a `0`, so a
97	  number like `121` looks loose at display sizes. Reserve
98	  `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for columns of numbers that must align
99	  vertically (table rows, axis ticks).
100	
101	## Texture - the backup channel (opt-in)
102	
103	Where hue fails - full-severity CVD, grayscale print, `forced-colors` - texture
104	carries identity. One directional hand-drawn fill, used at **45° and its 135° mirror
105	only** (never horizontal/vertical - those read as gridlines/bars). Inked tone-on-tone
106	(a step from the fill's own ramp), equal loudness across slots. On value scales the
107	texture is *ordered* (rotation steps with magnitude; arm angle carries the diverging
108	sign) so it never misstates the value. Triggered by an accessibility setting, print,
109	or `forced-colors` - never on by default. (See `palette.md`.)

1	# Interaction - tooltips & filters
2	
3	An HTML chart is interactive by default - the hover layer is part of the deliverable,
4	not an upgrade. Omitting it is the exception (a bare stat tile), never the default.
5	Design it with the same care as the static render.
6	
7	## Tooltips & hover
8	
9	Tooltips **enhance, they never gate**: every value a tooltip shows is also reachable
10	without it, through direct labels or the table view. Same details on keyboard focus
11	as on hover.
12	
13	- **The crosshair finds the X.** A vertical hairline tracks the pointer and snaps to
14	  the nearest data position. Readers aim at a date, never at a 2px line.
15	- **On bars and cells, the mark is the hit target.** No crosshair - each bar, segment,
16	  dot, or heat-cell carries its own `pointermove`/`focus` tooltip showing category and
17	  value, and the hovered mark lifts (slight lighten or outline) so the reader sees it respond.
18	- **One tooltip, every series.** The readout lists every series at that X - the
19	  pointer never has to land on a line or a fill to get a value.
20	- **Labels are untrusted data - use `textContent`.** Series and category names
21	  often come from CSV headers, tool output, or API responses. Insert them into
22	  tooltip/legend/table DOM with `textContent` or `createTextNode`, never via
23	  `innerHTML` string concatenation.
24	- **Values lead, labels follow.** In the tooltip the value is the Strong,
25	  high-contrast element and the series name is secondary - the legend's hierarchy
26	  inverted, because here the reader has the series and wants the number.
27	- **Line keys, not boxes.** Tooltip rows key their series with a short stroke of the
28	  series color; at tooltip density a filled box is data-weight ink doing a label's
29	  job. (Legends still mirror the mark: rect for bars/areas, line for lines.)
30	- **The hit target is bigger than the mark.** A mark's hover/focus area includes its
31	  2px surface gap and then some - never only the painted pixels. An 8px scatter dot is a
32	  pinpoint nobody hits reliably; give each point a transparent hit area of at least
33	  **24px**, or - for dense scatter - a nearest-point / Voronoi layer so the pointer only
34	  has to be *closest*, not dead-center. (The crosshair already does this for the X on
35	  line and bar charts; scatter and bubble need the per-point version.)
36	- **A value pushed off its mark lives in the tooltip.** When a label won't fit inside a
37	  small bar (see `marks-and-anatomy.md`), that bar's hit area carries the value on hover
38	  and focus - the tooltip is its overflow home, and the table view keeps it reachable
39	  without hovering at all.
40	
41	## Filters & time ranges
42	
43	Every monitoring dashboard needs the same controls. These are **standard UI, not
44	chart marks** - build them with ordinary HTML form controls styled to match the
45	chart chrome. Dataviz only adds composition rules:
46	
47	- **One row, above the charts.** Filters sit in a single left-aligned row above the
48	  content they scope - never inside a chart card, never per-chart. If one chart needs
49	  its own range, it's a different dashboard.
50	- **Date range first.** It's the filter every reader reaches for; presets (today,
51	  last 7 / 30 / 90 days) before a custom range.
52	- **Filters scope everything below them.** Every chart, stat, and table re-renders
53	  against the same slice, so the numbers always agree.
54	- **Refetch keeps the frame.** While data reloads, charts hold their previous render
55	  at reduced opacity - no skeleton, no layout jump, no flash.
56	
57	A good date picker lists presets as rows (nobody fights a calendar grid for "last 30
58	days"), marks selection with a 16px bold check, keeps hover a ghost wash so it never
59	competes with selection, and tucks the custom range behind a hairline in the footer.
60	(See `palette.md` for the reference spec.)
61

I have enough from dataviz. My widgets:

1. **KPI stat tiles** — label (sentence case), value (auto-compact), delta (signed, vs named period, color = direction × up-is-good; with icon since status/delta colors shouldn't be color-alone). No plot → no hover needed.
2. **Bar chart widget** — single series (one hue, blue). Columns ≤24px thick, 4px rounded data-end (top), square at baseline, grow from single baseline. Hairline gridlines recessive, y-axis ticks round clean numbers. Value on the cap selectively (maybe label max only... Actually "label selectively" — I'll label via hover tooltip per bar; maybe label each bar cap is "number on every point" → avoid. Just tooltip + axis ticks). Hover: per-bar tooltip showing category + value, bar lifts on hover. Hit target = the bar slot (wider than painted bar). Single series → no legend.
3. Maybe a **tall segmented bar** or progress/meter widget for variety — e.g., "Capacity used" meter: fill carries accent, track is lighter step of same ramp. That's a nice third widget type.
4. A list widget ("recent activity") — plain UI, no viz.
5. Title widget (pluginTitle) and text widget (pluginText).

Colors: single-series blue from validated palette: light `#2a78d6`, dark `#3987e5`. For the meter, same ramp track: track = lighter step of same ramp — light mode track `#cde2fb` (step 100) or maybe `#b7d3f6`; dark mode: lighter step relative to dark... dark series is `#3987e5` (step 400); track should be lighter step of same ramp — on dark, "lighter" visually... the ramp: for dark mode, steps like 250 `#86b6ef` is lighter. Hmm, on a dark surface a lighter track would glow. Actually the track convention in UI is a low-emphasis fill; the palette guidance: "the unfilled track is a lighter step of the same ramp (blue-on-blue)". For dark mode, use a darker step like 600 `#184f95`? The intent is track = receded version of fill hue. In dark mode, receded = darker. I'll use light-mode track `#cde2fb`, dark-mode track `#184f95` (darker step). Hmm — "lighter step of the same ramp" — in ramp numbering, lighter = lower step number (100 lightest). But on dark surface a near-white track is wrong. The palette file itself for dark surfaces steps darker. I'll choose: light track `#cde2fb`, dark track `#184f95`. That reads as "same hue, receded" in both modes.

Delta colors: delta up good (success text) light `#006300` / dark `#0ca30c`. Delta down = critical `#d03b3b` both modes (status). If up is bad (e.g., churn), invert. Use arrow icons + text (icon + label pairing).

Where do these colors come from given Gravity UI tokens? Gravity UI semantic tokens: `--g-color-text-positive` (light #3b9950? dark...), `--g-color-text-danger`. Hmm — the dataviz palette's delta-up-good is `#006300`. Gravity UI has its own positive/danger text tokens which are theme-aware. The dataviz skill says design system supplies parameters; Gravity UI's text-positive/danger tokens are the status colors here. Mixing: to stay consistent within Gravity UI, I should use `--g-color-text-positive` and `--g-color-text-danger` for deltas. That respects both skills: status colors with icon + label. Gravity's tokens are theme-aware and validated within the system. Similarly for series color — Gravity UI doesn't ship chart palette tokens in uikit (charts package has its own). For a single series, using `--g-color-base-brand`? No — brand blue in Gravity is fine as series-1 blue, but the dataviz default palette is validated `#2a78d6`/`#3987e5`. Gravity's `--g-color-base-brand` light is `#5282ff`... its contrast on white is ~2.9:1? Not sure. The safest per dataviz skill: use its validated values via CSS custom properties scoped to the viz, with dark values under Gravity's `.g-root_theme_dark` selector. For text, use Gravity tokens (`--g-color-text-secondary` etc.) — text tokens from the system are required by Gravity skill (semantic tokens rule). The dataviz skill says text wears text tokens — using the design system's text tokens is exactly right.

Actually the widget background: I'll render widgets on `--g-color-base-float` (standard card). Let me grep the token values.

tool.result:
## Color & encoding

**Bad: Dual-axis charts (two y-scales on one plot).**
Why it misleads: the alignment of the two scales is arbitrary, so the chart invents a
correlation that isn't in the data. Real example: an "Adoption" chart plotting Users
(0-30k) against Sessions (0-800k) - a reviewer flagged it as looking "hallucinated."
Good: Do instead: two charts, small multiples, or index both series to a common base
(=100 at t0) on **one** axis.

**Bad: Recolor-on-filter.** Assigning colors by current rank, so filtering out a series
repaints the survivors.
Why: a reader who learned "Acme is blue" is now misled.
Good: Color follows the entity, not its row number. Survivors keep their hue.

**Bad: Cycling / generating hues past 8.** A 9th categorical color, generated or reused.
Why: indistinguishable from an existing slot under CVD; breaks the order check.
Good: Fold the tail into "Other," facet into small multiples, or use composite encoding.

**Bad: Eyeballing colorblind-safety.** "These look different enough."
Good: Run `scripts/validate_palette.js`. Adjacent Delta E >= 8 (OKLab ×100), or 6-8 WITH secondary encoding.

**Bad: A value-ramp on nominal categories.** Coloring each bar darker-where-bigger
when the categories have no natural order (products, teams, endpoints).
Why: it double-encodes bar length as hue, burns the only free channel on
information the chart already shows, and fails the categorical checks by design
(a ramp spans the lightness band and drops below the chroma floor).
Good: One series -> one color (slot 1) for every bar. Ordered categories (funnel,
tiers, age bands) -> the ordinal ramp, validated with `--ordinal`.

**Bad: Rainbow / non-neighbor sequential.** A multi-hue ramp for magnitude.
Good: One hue, light->dark. (Analogous neighbors or semantic heat are the only multi-hue
sequential exceptions, always with a scale legend.)

**Bad: A hue at the diverging midpoint, or two cool hues as the two poles.**
Why: the midpoint must read as "nothing"; poles must read as opposite. blue<->aqua
fails this (both cool); blue<->red or blue<->orange succeed (warm/cool).
Good: Two hues that read as opposite + a neutral gray midpoint.

**Bad: Status color used for a non-status series** (or a series color used for status).
Good: Status tokens only when the color *means* good/bad; categorical when it's identity.

## Form

**Bad: Eight categorical hues when the story is one number.** The most common way a
chart misses its point.
Good: Emphasis (highlight one, gray the rest), or a stat tile / hero number.

**Bad: A one-bar bar chart, or a 2-slice pie.**
Good: A stat tile. The number is the chart.

**Bad: A donut/pie for comparing close values.**
Good: Ranked bars, or the numbers. Part-to-whole at a glance only, <= 6 segments: the tall
segmented bar (`choosing-a-form.md`).

**Bad: More than ~7 color classes carrying meaning.**
Good: A table, or table + chart. Past ~7 bins, adjacent classes blur.

## Marks & chrome

**Bad: Thick saturated blocks, heavy gridlines, no breathing room.** Reads loud, even
childish, at scale.
Good: Thin marks, hairline recessive grid/axes, generous padding. Saturated fills are
for small marks and accents, never large blocks.
**Exception:** the tall segmented bar (*Figures* in `marks-and-anatomy.md`).

**Bad: Dashed gridlines or axis rules.** Dashing adds visual noise and reads as
"projection" or "threshold" when it's just a grid.
Good: Gridlines and axes are solid hairlines, one shade off the surface.

**Bad: A number on every data point.** A value beside every dot or segment is chaos and goes unread.
Good: A legend is always present for >= 2 series; direct-label *selectively* (the endpoint, the extreme, the one series that matters) and let the axis + tooltip carry the rest.
**Exception:** the tall segmented bar (*Figures* in `marks-and-anatomy.md`).

**Bad: A border drawn around marks to separate them.**
Good: A 2px surface gap between fills (stacked segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring (on overlapping markers).

**Bad: A label clipped by, or overflowing, a too-small bar or stacked segment** -
including `overflow: hidden` cropping the first/last characters of an in-segment label.
Good: Only render a label inside a mark when it fits with padding; otherwise move it
outside the bar end, or drop it to the tooltip/legend (the value stays in the table view).

**Bad: A chart container whose fixed height excludes the x-axis band** - the plot
fits, the axis labels don't, so the card gets a tiny nested vertical scroll.
Good: Size the container to include the axis labels (plot height + x-axis band),
or let the container grow with its content instead of fixing a height.

**Bad: A display or serif face on the hero figure.** It reads as off-brand decoration.
Good: The hero figure uses the same sans as everything else.

**Bad: `tabular-nums` on a large standalone number.** Equal-width digits make `121`
look loose at display sizes.
Good: Proportional figures on hero and stat-tile values; `tabular-nums` only where
numbers align vertically (table rows, axis ticks).

**Bad: Texture on by default, or as decoration.** Dense angled fields are a vestibular
risk and read as noise on value scales.
Good: Texture is opt-in (a11y setting, print, forced-colors), 45°/135° only, ordered on
value scales.

## Interaction & accessibility

**Bad: A tooltip as the only way to read a value.**
Good: Tooltips enhance, never gate - every value is also reachable via direct labels or
the table view; keyboard focus shows the same as hover.

**Bad: Pinpoint hover targets - an 8px scatter dot you must land on dead-center.**
Good: The hit area includes the 2px gap and meets a ~24px minimum; dense scatter uses a nearest-point / Voronoi layer.

**Bad: Per-chart filters, or filters inside a chart card.**
Good: One filter row above everything it scopes; all charts re-render against the same slice.

**Bad: Skeleton flash on refetch.**
Good: Hold the previous render at reduced opacity - no layout jump.

Дашборд на **`@gravity-ui/dashkit`** (10.5.2, доустановлен вместе с `@gravity-ui/icons`) — виджеты свободно перетаскиваются и растягиваются по 36-колоночной сетке в режиме редактирования.

**Виджеты (плагины DashKit):**
- `title` — встроенный `pluginTitle`
- `stat` — KPI-плитка: метка, значение, дельта со стрелкой и именованным периодом (цвет = направление × «хорошо ли это», не цветом одним)
- `bars` — столбчатый график: одна серия → один валидированный оттенок синего, столбцы ≤24px со скруглённым верхом, тонкие сеточные линии, «чистые» тики оси, тултип по hover/focus на каждом слоте (hit-target — весь слот, не только столбец)
- `meter` — шкала квоты: заливка серией, трек — светлый шаг той же рампы, `role="meter"`
- `list` — лента событий со скроллом внутри виджета

**Каркас:** шапка с переключателем «Редактирование» (`Switch`), меню «Виджет» (`DropdownMenu`, добавление через `DashKit.setItem` с явной позицией внизу сетки — так в localStorage не попадает `Infinity`), сброс раскладки, переключатель светлой/тёмной темы через вложенный `ThemeProvider scoped rootClassName="app"` (main.tsx не тронут). Раскладка сохраняется в `localStorage` и переживает перезагрузку. В оверлей-меню виджета оставлен только пункт «удалить» (копированию не к чему без ActionPanel).

**Палитра графика** проверена скриптом `validate_palette.js` против реальных поверхностей Gravity (`#ffffff` / `#383438` из `--g-color-base-float`) — оба режима PASS; тёмные значения заданы под `.g-root_theme_dark`. Текст/линии — только семантические `--g-color-*`, отступы/радиусы — `--g-spacing-*` / `--g-border-radius-*`.

## Проверки

- ✅ `tsc --noEmit` — чисто (одна правка: `Text color="inherit"` не существует в uikit 7.43 → `positive`/`danger`)
- ✅ `vite build` — успешно
- ✅ Чек-лист anti-patterns dataviz-скилла пройден (одна серия — один цвет, нет подписи на каждой точке, тонкие метки, тултип не единственный путь к значению)

**Что typecheck не покрывает — стоит глянуть глазами** (`npm run dev`): обе темы, узкий (~375px) и широкий (~1400px) вьюпорты, перетаскивание/ресайз в режиме редактирования и поведение добавленных виджетов после перезагрузки.
